subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should this issue be scoped to Telegram/media dropped-attachment diagnostics while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 owns configurable host media roots, or should this issue also define the root-expansion contract?
rationale: The diagnostic half is a bounded bug, but accepting more absolute host paths changes a public config and security boundary, so automation should not choose that product contract.

options.title: Diagnostics Here, Roots In Canonical Issue
options.body: Keep this issue focused on warn-level reason logging and optional user-visible unavailable-attachment text, while the related open issue owns configurable roots.

options.title: Use This Issue For Root Policy
options.body: Let this issue define the permanent host-media-root contract and close or retarget overlapping root-policy reports after maintainer approval.

options.title: Document Managed Roots Only
options.body: Decline new root expansion for now and update docs to state that arbitrary host paths must be staged into managed roots or sent through an explicit message-tool path.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics Here, Roots In Canonical Issue
recommendation.body: Keep this issue focused on warn-level reason logging and optional user-visible unavailable-attachment text, while the related open issue owns configurable roots.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on outbound media access policy and root plumbing.
